correctness.rationale: For each parent, disjoint child supports make S*S diagonal. Positive spine column norm=1 for m>=1 and >=1 for m<=0, unary tooth norm >=1; bounded and left invertible. Exact spine product sqrt(N/(N+m)); new tooth relative squared ratio (1/N)g_m with g_m=(1+m/N)^beta; dual ratio 1/(N g_m). Therefore primal sum diverges always, dual sum diverges iff beta<=1 by the p-series, satisfying cited Chavan–Trivedi rootless Wold criterion. Independently checked the orthogonal-column singular-value multiset: positive-spine squares 2(1-sqrt((N+m-1)/(N+m))), negative spine 1/(N+1+|m|), each m>=2 tooth m-1 copies of [(1+m/N)^(beta/(2(m-1)))-1]^2. The two spine p-sums converge iff p>2 and each tends to N^(1-p/2)/(p/2-1); the tooth sum is O(N^(2-p)) when p>2, giving 4/(p-2). Largest column yields ||K||~N^-1/2. No inference of infinite-dimensional convergence from finite checker samples; the cited theorem remains an external analytic premise.
